name: Gapminder
description_short: Free interactive data tools and teaching materials from an independent educational non-profit: bubble charts, slides and videos, plus Dollar Street, photographs of everyday life in homes on different income levels around the world. Good for sparking discussion, comparing lifestyles and challenging assumptions.
teacher_note: Show two Dollar Street homes at different income levels and have students describe and compare them before they see any numbers.
creator: Gapminder
internal_notes: Facts checked 2026-11-05 against gapminder.org: Gapminder describes itself as an independent educational non-profit fighting global misconceptions (homepage, About); the Teaching Materials page (/teaching/materials/) lists Dollar Street, Bubble Charts and other Gapminder Tools charts, offline tools, slides, a poster and videos, and says the tools and teaching materials are free and always will be. Dollar Street (/dollar-street/about) says it shows everyday life in homes on all income levels across the world; its own page gives two different counts (264 homes in 50 countries in the body, 468 families in 67 countries in the footer), so no count is used here. NOT stated by Gapminder, so not claimed: age groups, CEFR level, worksheets, lesson plans. Licence: Dollar Street images are stated as CC BY 4.0 with no credit wording given; no licence is stated for the slides or videos. No Gapminder images are used on this site (the thumbnail is a typographic card). age_group, cefr_level and group_fit left unknown rather than guessed. The URL is the Teaching Materials page, the most useful page for teachers; the main site is https://www.gapminder.org/.
